Harbour lights return to Brindle Quay

By Odile Marchetti · 14 March 2026

The row of brass harbour lamps that once lined Brindle Quay will be lit again this weekend, eleven years after the last of them was removed for repairs that never happened.

The council voted on Tuesday to release the remaining restoration budget, enough for twenty-two lamps. Volunteers from the Quay Preservation Society have spent the winter cataloguing the original fittings, which were found in a warehouse behind the old ferry office.

What happens on Saturday

At dusk the mayor will light the first lamp by hand, as the harbour master did every evening until 2015. Local bakeries are planning a lantern walk, and the ferry company has promised a late sailing so passengers can see the quay from the water.

Society chair Henrik Doyle said the work was never about nostalgia. "The lamps are part of how boats find the channel in fog," he said. "We just forgot that."

The cost

The restoration came to 184,000 pounds, of which 61,000 came from donations. The council expects running costs of roughly 3,200 pounds a year.
